title: Walks in the local area
titleCn: 本地徒步路线推荐：Village Walk、McGrady Falls 与煤矿步道

paragraphs.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions one to six.
G'day. What can I do for you?
I'd like to do a day's walk in the area. Do you have any suggestions?

Well, the most popular day walks around here are the Village Walk, the McGrady Falls Trail, and the Coal Mine Walk. If you just want a short walk, you can do the Village Walk. That's just 6 kilometers. The McGrady Falls is 12 kilometers. The Coal Mine Walk's a bit longer again. It's 13.5.
Right. So are those two more difficult as well as longer?

Well, the Village Walk's classified as easy. McGrady Falls has some climbing, which is a bit difficult, but overall it's moderate. But the Coal Mine Walk's mostly on flat ground, and the paths are very good, so that's down as easy in spite of the length.
And, um, what's special about each of the walks? I mean, what interesting things could I see?
Well, with the Village Walk, you start off in the village. It's really nice. And right in the middle, there's the museum. That's very popular. It tells you a bit about the background to the region.
Okay.

Then at the edge of the village, there's a park where you can have a rest and look at the view before you set off on the walk back. It's pretty impressive on a clear day. You get a fantastic view of the mountains.
Mm.
I wouldn't mind a chance to go swimming. Can I do that at the McGrady Falls?

Yeah, just under the falls there's a great pool. At this time of year, it's quite chilly, but it's a good way of cooling off after the climb up. And if you're interested in flowers, it's a really good walk. You'll see lots of them.
Oh, right. And the Coal Mine Walk? Do you actually go down a mine?

No, it's closed down now, but there are signs along the path telling you all about the mine's history. It's very popular with school parties, but it's not just aimed at children. It's interesting for anyone.
Well, it sounds good, but I think I'll go for the McGrady Falls Trail.
Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions seven to ten.
Now listen and answer questions seven to ten.
Is there anything else I should know about it? Things to take and so on?

Well, I should tell you there's an entrance fee for the trail, for maintenance, et cetera. It's, uh, ten dollars for adults, and you'll need a map because the walk's not guided, but they'll give you one when you pay your entry fee.
Right. And I'd like to take a picnic.
The best thing is to get that from the cafe at the beginning of the trail. They'll pack it all up for you.
Great. And can you tell me how to get there?
Sure. The start of the trail is about 9 kilometers from here, so it's best to get a bus.
Will the bus that stops at the front of the hotel take me there?

That's the number 268 bus. It wouldn't take you there directly. It's best if you walk down to the market, and then you can catch the number 279 there. It'll take you directly to the start of the trail.
Okay. And will it be easy to tell when to get off?
You need to ask the bus driver to stop at the lake.
Mm-hmm.
The start of the walk is just beyond that.
Okay. And the trail is a round trip?
Yes, so you can get the same bus back. But mind that you're not too late. The last bus leaves at 5:30 on weekdays and 6:30 on Saturdays and 6 o'clock on Sundays.
Okay. Well, thanks for all that information.
No problems. Have a good walk.
That is the end of part one. You now have one minute to check your answers to part one.
